prose.md:
**As of 2026-09-11 15:45.** Only what is queued, running or next. Finished jobs live on their `todo` row.

## Running — the SIGReg pool pair at tc1536

`BSC:45665286` finished 09-11 14:24 — the tc512 detach arm reached **ep 100/100**, exit `0:0`, `epoch_100.pth` on disk, and `todo/13` is closed ([the read](results/2026-09-11_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc512_ep100_slides.html)).

Both pool arms started **09-11 15:35** and are past the first-iteration check: `Training (Epoch 0)` on both, 0.99 s/iter over 2250 iters, so **~37 min/epoch** and **ep 4 lands ~18:20 today**. 20 h wall reaches ~ep 32.

## The pair

One variable. Both `sigreg_weight` 0.02, both `sw0`, both 20 h on `ehpc1001`, both from the unchanged no-bottleneck script.
`RUN_NAME`s differ only in the pool tag.

| Job | `sigreg_pool_samples` | `scale = n_pooled/n_live` | TODO | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BSC:45725881 | **8192** | 11.7 | `todo/14` | RUNNING on `as03r2b16`, train loss 0.739 at iter 60 |
| BSC:45727710 | **24576** | **33.0** | `todo/14` | RUNNING on `as04r3b15`, train loss 0.855 at iter 60 |

`RUN_NAME`s verified to differ only in the pool tag: `..._sigreg0.02_ns3072_pool8192_compose1.0_decnoise0.8_detach_sw0` against `..._pool24576_...`.

Motivated by the finite-sample floor: at S=8192 it is 1.32e-4 against a 1.65e-4 anisotropy signal, so SIGReg can barely see a rank collapse at Cz=1536.
**Guard** — `analysis/2026-07-31_sigreg_pool_not_weight_neutral.html` found pool 32768 at unchanged weight stalled training outright. Compare Eval `LossRecon` at **ep 4**; if `45727710` sits near 0.126 while `45725881` has broken out, kill it.
That failure spiked at the `sigreg_warmup=2000` boundary, which `sw0` removes — so it may not reproduce.

## Next

| Do | TODO | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Train the **flow** on the tc512 detached tokenizer, from its final `epoch_100.pth` | `todo/13` → `flow` | **ungated — the checkpoint exists.** Nothing is submitted for it yet |
| Read the pool pair at ep ~29 | `todo/14` | both running since 15:35; the ep-4 guard first, ~18:20 today |
| Submit the OpenScene arm — code implemented, md5-matched on BSC | `todo/13` | none |

Two tc1536 arms cancelled in two days, both for the regulariser. `BSC:45610897` on 09-10 11:47 at ep 31/100: [the read](results/2026-09-10_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc1536_read_slides.html) found `z` stuck at `ZPartRank` 1.0.
`BSC:45678654` on **09-11 11:20 at ep 23/100**: [the read](results/2026-09-11_tc_width_bneck_sw0_tc1536_read_slides.html) showed the forced bottleneck cures the code and costs **×3.2** the token recon.
Against the tc512 detach arm the gap is **rank, not scale** — both sit at RMS ≈ 1, but tc512 grows to 57 usable dims of 512 while the bneck arm shrinks to 35 of 1536. `sigreg_weight` is the least likely cause; `force_bottleneck` at `z_dim == hidden_size` builds a **square** `Linear(1536,1536)`, which pins scale but imposes no dimensional pressure.

todos.item: End-to-end noisy-channel tokenizer at tc512: fold z + σ·ε into training with the encoder in the graph

plan/2026-09-07_tc_width_decnoise_e2e_tc512.md. Routed here by falsifier 3 of TODO 12's plan: "the pair needs a from-scratch noisy tokenizer, which changes z and is a tc_width/sigreg question, not a flow one." Motivation: the cov_weight dose-response (TODO 6) shows train ZPartRank monotone in dose to 141.0 with none of it transferring to recon, so a term that pushes E[zzᵀ]→I is answered; a noisy channel applies the pressure through the reconstruction loss instead. Control throughout is the clean twin BSC:45296347. The full-width arm split off 2026-09-10 into TODO 14.

In-graph arm BSC:45529827, cancelled 2026-09-08 at ep 39/100 — negative. The encoder is in the graph, so it optimises a code that must survive the channel while SIGReg and the compose sum keep reading the clean z. Read at ep 37 (results/2026-09-08_tc_width_decnoise_e2e_tc512_read_slides.html): Eval/Loss +28.1% at matched epoch and ZPartRank halved (40.3 vs 78.7) — a fixed absolute σ is answered with a 1.91× larger z, buying tolerance with scale rather than dimensions. The in-graph mode is removed from the code, not gated, so BSC:45529827 must not be resumed against current code.

Detached arm BSC:45578805 — answers the question yes (plan/2026-09-08_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc512.md, read 2026-09-10 in results/2026-09-10_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc512_slides.html). A second decode of z.detach() + σ·ε with its own loss leaves encoder gradients identical to the clean twin. At matched 60 ep Eval/Loss is 0.0456 vs the twin's 0.0451 (+1.1%, against the in-graph arm's +26.2%); ZPartRank 79.5/97.9 vs 86.9/97.1 and z scale back on the SIGReg anchor — both in-graph pathologies vanish once the encoder is off the hook, so the ep-37 mechanism is confirmed by removal. Ladder measured on both epoch_60.pth with --eval-only (BSC:45663648 twin, BSC:45664038 detached, same seeded ε; the twin predates eval_noise_sigmas and had never had one): at σ=0.82 the detached arm's penalty is 2.4× smaller on both sets (23.3% vs 56.3% KITTI, 25.5% vs 61.2% nuScenes), −19.4% / −22.2% absolute. Cost +9.7% wall clock (38.3 vs 34.9 min/ep). Rank never climbs above the twin, so the ~90/512 shelf has now resisted three axes and is retired as a tc_width lever. σ stays absolute here, so the "σ must go relative" finding from the ep-37 read is untouched.

Closed 2026-09-11 at ep 100/100. BSC:45578805 stopped clean at ep 62 on one 40 h allocation and was chained 2026-09-10 as BSC:45665286, which resumed current.pth at Training (Epoch 62) and reached training.epoch=100 in 23 h 57 m — COMPLETED, exit 0:0, 24.0 h of a 40 h wall, epoch_100.pth (8.19 GB) on disk. Read in results/2026-09-11_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc512_ep100_slides.html. Nothing the ep-60 read said changed: at the twin's last matched epoch 82 the clean cost is +2.7% KITTI / −0.3% nuScenes (+1.5% pooled, against +1.1% pooled at ep 60), and the last 18 epochs buy only −0.8%, so the arm is converged. ZPartRank closes at 83.8/512 against the twin's 92.0 and has been flat since ep 60 — the ~90/512 shelf holds at 100 epochs too. Two things the ep-60 read could not see. First, decoded the sign flips: on KITTI the arm beats the clean twin on PredVsOrig depth (−4.1%) and pointmap (−4.4%) and on PredVsGT depth (−2.5%), losing only raymap (+7.5% / +4.4% on both sets), so token LossRecon is the wrong single number to rank these two arms by. Second, the σ ladder ratio widens with training — the arm's own σ=0.82 penalty goes +17.5% at ep 40 to +27.1% at ep 100 — because the noised decode converges about 40 epochs before the clean one does (KITTI σ=0.82 absolute 0.0671 → 0.0661 while clean goes 0.0544 → 0.0520). The "2.4× smaller than the twin" figure therefore holds only at the epoch both were measured at, and any future twin comparison has to be epoch-matched. Left open: the flow re-read on this tokenizer, the only test the noise tolerance is actually for — it trains on epoch_100.pth, not epoch_60.pth; and σ stays absolute, so "σ must go relative" is still unanswered.

todos.item: Detached decoder-noise at full width (tc1536, no channel bottleneck), and the unnormalised z it exposed
todos.note:
plan/2026-09-09_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc1536.md. Split out of TODO 13 on 2026-09-10, which had grown to cover two questions: 13 owns the noise recipe at tc512, this row owns full width and the code scale it exposed. The arm is the tc512 detached-noise recipe with no channel bottleneck — target_channels=1536 == hidden_size, sigreg_num_slices 3072 (2·Cz), sigreg_weight 0.06 (∝ Cz from the tc512 twin's 0.02), pool 8192 unchanged. Submitted 2026-09-09 as BSC:45608142 (ehpc880), which died at 43 min on a transient cusolverDnCreate failure — not a config bug — and was resubmitted as BSC:45610897.

Read at ep 31 (results/2026-09-10_tc_width_decnoise_detach_tc1536_read_slides.html): width wins, the recipe costs, the code is stuck. Removing the tc512 bottleneck is worth −51.6% / −49.2% LossRecon at matched ep 31, and tc512 cannot close it with 2× the epochs (its ep 61 0.0542 is still 1.83× this arm's ep 31). But the 2026-08 plain tc1536 reference BSC:44590128 (sigreg 0.005, no decnoise) beats this arm at every epoch on every readout — +17.0% KITTI / +25.4% nuScenes — so width buys the 2× and the decnoise + 12× sigreg recipe gives a quarter of it back. The plan's over-regularisation guard passes (train recon 0.51× the twin, raw SIGReg: descending to 0.0014) and is the wrong instrument: ZPartRank sits at 1.0/1536 with ZRowMeanSquare 872 the whole time.

Diagnosis — a sparse heavy tail, not a collapsed code. Simulation at the real Cz=1536 geometry fits all four scalars only one way: the tail sits on a single coordinate channel, ~0.57% of rows at ~1.5e4. A random direction reads ZMeanAbsMax 8.1 against the observed 87.7, and a broad collapse is excluded by 900× on the SIGReg statistic. That is the massive-activation / attention-sink signature. SIGReg is structurally unable to see it: the statistic is a bounded mean of cos/sin over rows, so a 0.5% tail moves it by nothing, while ZPartRank is a second moment and the same 0.5% owns the entire trace. It cannot pull the tail back either — the restoring force on an outlier row goes as p·exp(−p²/4), coherent only for |p| ≲ 5. No sigreg_weight fixes this; it is structural, not a tuning miss.

Why tc1536 and never tc512: pre_bottleneck_norm and z_proj_down are built only when z_dim != hidden_size (deltatok_trainer.py:151) and z_norm=false makes the final norm an nn.Identity (:184), so at tc1536 with _nozn nothing normalises z anywhere; tc512 keeps a LayerNorm pinning z_proj_down's input to unit variance. LeJEPA never meets this because its scale is fixed upstream and not by SIGReg — backbone LayerNorm, projector BatchNorm1ds, weight decay 5e-2, and lamb constant from step 0.

BSC:45610897 cancelled 2026-09-10 11:47 at ep 31/100 (21.4 h) rather than chained — chaining a stuck arm buys nothing. Successor submitted the same day as BSC:45678654 (plan/2026-09-10_tc_width_bneck_sw0_tc1536.md): a new force_bottleneck flag builds tc512's three modules at tc1536 — LayerNorm(1536) + Linear(1536,1536) down/up, ~4.7 M params — with sigreg_warmup=0, so the code is normalised and the anchor is on from step 0. The flag defaults false and builds nothing, so every other arm stays bit-identical. The detached noise term is not a suspect: it decodes z.detach(), so it has no gradient path to the encoder and cannot push z outward — what still separates the two tc1536 arms is 12× the sigreg weight (0.06 vs 0.005) and this norm. Read at ep 4, the epoch where the plain arm escapes ZPartRank 1.0 and BSC:45610897 never did.

Read at ep 22 (results/2026-09-11_tc_width_bneck_sw0_tc1536_read_slides.html): the code is cured and the decoder pays 3.2x for it. Every mechanical check held - pre_bottleneck_norm 0.003M + z_proj_down 2.361M + z_proj_up 2.361M = 4.725M of 685.757M, sigreg_warmup=0 in EXTRA_CFG, ZRowMeanSquare 1.02 on the first eval - and ZPartRank never touches 1.0, so the ep-4 gate passes and the ep-31 massive-activation diagnosis is confirmed by repair. ZRowMeanSquare 1.13 against the control's 2781, ZMeanAbsMax 0.10 against 171.

It is not enough and it is expensive. At matched ep 22 token LossRecon is x3.24 / x3.11 the control (0.1054 / 0.0722 vs 0.0325 / 0.0232), x3.72 / x3.80 the plain tc1536 BSC:44590128 and x1.56 the detached tc512 arm BSC:45665286 at half the width; decoded, pointmap PredVsOrig is x4.35 KITTI / x6.62 nuScenes and the rollout is worse. The arm never has the ep-4 cliff the other three have - it descends 0.134 to 0.105 over 19 epochs and stays on the plateau. Rank lands at 2.3% of Cz against the plain arm's 15.7%, and the raw SIGReg statistic is 4x further from the anchor than the control's (0.0063 vs 0.0016) at the same weight and slice count: scale fixed, rank not. The sigma ladder is flat (+0.3% at sigma=0.82, where the control pays +55% and tc512 +12%) on a code of RMS 1.13 - a decoder undisturbed by noise the size of its own input is not reading much of it.

The missing norm was not the cause. The plain tc1536 has no norm on z either, sits at ZPartRank 1.0 for epochs 1-3 and escapes on its own at ep 4 (44.2, 112.8, 172.4, 240.7 by ep 22), so what traps the control is not the missing norm but the 12x sigreg weight and the decode-noise term. Next arm: tc1536, no bottleneck, sigreg_weight 0.005, decnoise on - one 40 h allocation, tests that suspect directly. Caveat: this arm moved force_bottleneck and sigreg_warmup together, so the read cannot assign the recon damage to either alone.

BSC:45678654 cancelled 2026-09-11 11:20 at ep 23/100 (15.2 h) - sigreg pressure too high. The read had already answered the plan's question and the arm was 3.2x off the control with 24 h of its wall left; spending them to reach ~ep 63 on a decoder that is not reading its code buys nothing. Surviving on SCRATCH/deltatok_log/<run>/ckpts/: current.pth (ep 23), epoch_20.pth, epoch_10.pth, 31 G. Relaunching this slurm script resumes it - training always picks up current.pth, so the successor needs a new RUN_NAME. Next arm: tc1536, no bottleneck, sigreg_weight 0.005, decnoise on.

Sigreg-weight sweep submitted 2026-09-11 11:42 - BSC:45725879 (0.005), BSC:45725880 (0.01), BSC:45725881 (0.02), all on ehpc1001 at 20 h each, from the unchanged slurm/deltatok/train_deltatok_compose_sigreg_decnoise_detach_nozn_tc1536_bsc.slurm with --export=ALL,SIGREG_WEIGHT=<w>,SIGREG_WARMUP=0,RUN_NAME=<...>_sw0. No file edit: the script already derives RUN_NAME from the weight, and the explicit RUN_NAME only adds the _sw0 tag the plain script omits. sigreg_warmup is 0 - the anchor is on from step 0 on every arm, standing policy. A first submission at the script's default warmup 2000 (45725787/88/89) was cancelled while still PENDING, so nothing was written. Against the control BSC:45610897 (0.06, warmup 2000) weight and warmup both differ; the clean single-variable comparison is within the sweep. 20 h is ~29 epochs at the control's 41 min/ep, past the ep-4 cliff and onto the plateau. A no-decnoise partner already exists at every weight - sigreg 0.005/0.01/0.02 ns3072 pool8192 at ep 48 / 30 / 40 - so each arm reads as decnoise on vs off at matched weight, and ep 30 is a matched point for all three.

Sweep cut to a pool pair, 2026-09-11 12:10. BSC:45725879 (0.005) and BSC:45725880 (0.01) cancelled while PENDING; nothing was written. What runs is a one-variable pool comparison at sigreg_weight 0.02, both sw0, both 20 h on ehpc1001, both from the unchanged no-bottleneck script: BSC:45725881 at sigreg_pool_samples 8192 and BSC:45727710 at 24576. RUN_NAMEs differ only in pool8192 vs pool24576.

Known risk, accepted. analysis/2026-07-31_sigreg_pool_not_weight_neutral.html found pool 8192->32768 at unchanged weight *stopped* DeltaTok learning (Eval/Loss stuck at the untrained 0.126 through ep 11 against a twin at 0.0332 by ep 4), and reweighting at 0.05 / 0.5 / 5 did not rescue it. Cause: scale = n_pooled/n_live (deltatok_trainer.py:701) cancels the instantaneous 1/n attenuation but not the FIFO's feedback delay, so SIGReg dominates the grad norm and grad_clip=0.1 starves recon. At our geometry scale is 11.7 at pool 8192 and 33.0 at 24576 (43.7 at the 32768 that failed). But that failure's signature was a 39x LossSIGReg spike at iter 2211, exactly where sigreg_warmup=2000 ended - and these arms run sw0, so that boundary does not exist. The follow-up BSC:44014668 that would have settled it is archived CANCELLED at 00:00:00, never run.

Guard: compare Eval LossRecon at ep 4. If 45727710 is still near 0.126 while 45725881 has broken out, it is the 2026-07-31 stall - kill it.

Why the bneck arm loses to the tc512 arm: rank, not scale, and probably not sigreg_weight (2026-09-11). Both sit at ZRowMeanSquare ~ 1 (1.27 vs 1.57 KITTI ep 22) and at a comparable raw SIGReg statistic (0.0114 vs 0.0141), so neither the scale-escape story nor "more pressure" separates them. What separates them is absolute usable dimensions: bneck goes ZPartRank 54.3 -> 34.7 of 1536 over ep 0->22 while tc512 goes 14.2 -> 57.1 of 512. Variance per used direction moves the opposite way too - bneck 28.7 -> 56.1 (concentrating), tc512 39.5 -> 14.1 (spreading). The wide arm ends with a *narrower* code than the narrow arm, and its sigma ladder (+0.3% vs +12.3%) says the decoder stopped reading it.

sigreg_weight is the least likely cause, on sign. SIGReg exists to *raise* rank; the arm with 3x the weight has *lower* absolute rank. Two better candidates. But the 2026-08 **plain** tc1536 reference `BSC:44590128` (sigreg 0.005, no decnoise) beats this arm at every epoch on every readout — **+17.0% KITTI / +25.4% nuScenes** — so width buys the 2× and the decnoise + 12× sigreg recipe gives a quarter of it back. **Diagnosis — a sparse heavy tail, not a collapsed code.** Simulation at the real Cz=1536 geometry fits all four scalars only one way: the tail sits on a **single coordinate channel**, ~0.57% of rows at ~1.5e4. A random direction reads `ZMeanAbsMax` 8.1 against the observed 87.7, and a broad collapse is excluded by 900× on the SIGReg statistic. That is the **massive-activation / attention-sink** signature. **SIGReg is structurally unable to see it**: the statistic is a bounded mean of `cos`/`sin` over rows, so a 0.5% tail moves it by nothing, while `ZPartRank` is a second moment and the same 0.5% owns the entire trace. It cannot pull the tail back either — the restoring force on an outlier row goes as `p·exp(−p²/4)`, coherent only for `|p| ≲ 5`. No `sigreg_weight` fixes this; it is structural, not a tuning miss.

**Why tc1536 and never tc512:** `pre_bottleneck_norm` and `z_proj_down` are built only when `z_dim != hidden_size` (`deltatok_trainer.py:151`) and `z_norm=false` makes the final norm an `nn.Identity` (`:184`), so at tc1536 with `_nozn` **nothing normalises `z` anywhere**; tc512 keeps a LayerNorm pinning `z_proj_down`'s input to unit variance. LeJEPA never meets this because its scale is fixed upstream and not by SIGReg — backbone `LayerNorm`, projector `BatchNorm1d`s, weight decay 5e-2, and `lamb` constant from step 0.

**`BSC:45610897` cancelled 2026-09-10 11:47 at ep 31/100 (21.4 h)** rather than chained — chaining a stuck arm buys nothing. The flag defaults `false` and builds nothing, so every other arm stays bit-identical. The detached noise term is **not** a suspect: it decodes `z.detach()`, so it has no gradient path to the encoder and cannot push `z` outward — what still separates the two tc1536 arms is **12× the sigreg weight** (0.06 vs 0.005) and this norm. **Read at ep 4**, the epoch where the plain arm escapes `ZPartRank` 1.0 and `BSC:45610897` never did.

Rank lands at **2.3% of Cz** against the plain arm's 15.7%, and the raw `SIGReg:` statistic is **4× further from the anchor** than the control's (0.0063 vs 0.0016) at the same weight and slice count: **scale fixed, rank not.** The σ ladder is **flat** (+0.3% at σ=0.82, where the control pays +55% and tc512 +12%) on a code of RMS 1.13 — a decoder undisturbed by noise the size of its own input is not reading much of it.
